2607.00870.title: Dynamic Bidirectional Pattern Memory: A Production-Scale Empirical Characterisation of Inference-Time Gating in Clinical NLP
2607.00870.paper_summary: We study inference-time pattern-memory gating in a production-scale clinical natural language processing (NLP) pipeline. The pipeline pairs a generator (Llama-3.3 70B) proposing extractions with a verifier (MMed-Llama-3.1 70B) accepting or rejecting them, over 167,034 PMC-Patients narratives, and adds a lightweight memory that learns at deployment which extractions to filter, so the verifier need not re-examine candidates already seen to fail. We report four findings. First, learning filtering rules directly from the verifier's rejections failed at full scale: the relation-extraction filter stayed empty despite 785,797 logged rejections, because they were spread too thinly across too many distinct forms to accumulate. Second, a simpler rule using a fixed clinical ontology produced the same filtering without the verifier, capturing 49,734 ontology-violating relations on a held-out 5,000-patient set. Third, of five versions of the question-answering filter, four failed for distinct, instructive reasons; the fifth succeeded by checking whether a patient's extracted entities support the question asked, and where it applies was 1.84 times likelier to flag an answer the verifier would reject than one it would accept. Fourth, one pattern held across all five: a filter is selective only when it tests the same evidence the verifier weighs, not when it imitates the verifier's output. Together these give a transferable result for any generator-verifier pipeline: the most natural memory design can fail silently at scale, and whether a pre-generation gate is selective is decided before any engineering effort, by whether its signal probes the question the verifier itself answers. Throughout, the system flags suspect extractions rather than deleting them, so every decision stays visible for clinical review. All code and test artefacts are released openly.
2607.00870.paper_summary_zh: 我們研究了在生產規模的臨床自然語言處理 (NLP) 管道中的推斷時模式記憶閘。<lb/>該管道將一個生成器 (Llama-3.3 70B) 提出的提取與一個驗證器 (MMed-Llama-3.1 70B) 接受或拒絕它們進行配對，涵蓋 167,034 個 PMC-Patients 敘述，並添加了一個輕量級的記憶體，該記憶體在部署時學習過濾哪些提取，因此驗證器不必重新檢查已經被拒絕的候選項。<lb/>我們報告了四個發現。<lb/>首先，直接從驗證器的拒絕中學習過濾規則在全規模下失敗：關係提取過濾器保持空白，儘管記錄了 785,797 次拒絕，因為它們分散在太多不同的形式中，無法累積。<lb/>第二，使用固定臨床本體的簡單規則在沒有驗證器的情況下產生了相同的過濾，捕獲了 49,734 個違反本體的關係，這是在保留的 5,000 名患者集上進行的。<lb/>第三，在五個版本的問答過濾器中，四個因不同的、具啟發性的原因而失敗；第五個通過檢查患者提取的實體是否支持所提問的問題而成功，並且在適用的情況下，其標記一個驗證器會拒絕的答案的可能性是標記一個驗證器會接受的答案的 1.84 倍。<lb/>第四，所有五個模式中都有一個共同點：過濾器只有在測試驗證器權衡的相同證據時才是選擇性的，而不是模仿驗證器的輸出。<lb/>這些結果共同為任何生成器-驗證器管道提供了一個可轉移的結果：最自然的記憶設計在規模上可能會靜默失敗，而預生成閘是否具選擇性是在任何工程努力之前決定的，取決於其信號是否探測到驗證器自己回答的問題。<lb/>在整個過程中，系統標記可疑的提取，而不是刪除它們，因此每個決策對臨床審查保持可見。<lb/>所有代碼和測試工件均公開發布。
2607.00870.author: Ali H. Lazem et.al.
